financial_analyst.statement_analysis:
### NVIDIA CORP (NVDA): fiscal year ended 2026-01-25 (fiscal 2026)

All fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2025 figures come from 10-K 0001045810-26-000021, filed 2026-02-25. Fiscal 2026 runs 2025-01-27 to 2026-01-25. Fiscal 2025 runs 2024-01-29 to 2025-01-26. Amounts are in $ millions, except per share. The code computed every ratio; I copied each one as given.

#### Growth (fiscal 2026 over fiscal 2025)
| Line | FY2026 | FY2025 | Growth | Arithmetic | Source (tag) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total revenue | $215,938.0 million | $130,497.0 million | 65.47% | 215,938.0 / 130,497.0 - 1 | us-gaap:Revenues |
| Operating income | $130,387.0 million | $81,453.0 million | 60.08% | 130,387.0 / 81,453.0 - 1 | us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss |
| Net income attributable to the company | $120,067.0 million | $72,880.0 million | 64.75% | 120,067.0 / 72,880.0 - 1 | us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss |
| Diluted EPS (GAAP) | $4.90 | $2.94 | 66.67% | 4.90 / 2.94 - 1 | us-gaap:EarningsPerShareDiluted |
| Cash from operations | $102,718.0 million | $64,089.0 million | 60.27% | 102,718.0 / 64,089.0 - 1 | us-gaap:NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities |
| Additions to property and equipment | $6,042.0 million | $3,236.0 million | 86.71% | 6,042.0 / 3,236.0 - 1 | us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets |

Revenue grew 65.47%, faster than operating income at 60.08%. Diluted EPS grew 66.67%, a little faster than net income at 64.75%. Capital spending grew fastest of all lines, at 86.71%.

#### Margins
| Ratio | FY2026 | FY2025 | Arithmetic (FY2026; FY2025) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operating margin | 60.38% | 62.42% | 130,387.0 / 215,938.0; 81,453.0 / 130,497.0 |
| Net margin | 55.60% | 55.85% | 120,067.0 / 215,938.0; 72,880.0 / 130,497.0 |

Operating margin narrowed from 62.42% to 60.38% because operating income grew more slowly than revenue. Net margin was almost unchanged: 55.60% against 55.85%.

#### Returns on equity
- **Return on average equity, FY2026: 101.49%.** Arithmetic: 120,067.0 / ((157,293.0 + 79,327.0) / 2).
  - Inputs: net income from us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss, 2025-01-27 to 2026-01-25. Stockholders' equity of $157,293.0 million at 2026-01-25 and $79,327.0 million at 2025-01-26, from us-gaap:StockholdersEquity.
- Equity nearly doubled during the year. Return on year-end equity would therefore be noticeably lower than the average-equity figure. I have requested it in calculator_requests and did not compute it here.

#### Leverage
- **Debt to equity, FY2026: 0.054.** Arithmetic: (7,469.0 + 999.0) / 157,293.0.
  - Long-term debt of $7,469.0 million comes from us-gaap:LongTermDebtNoncurrent at 2026-01-25.
  - Current portion of $999.0 million comes from us-gaap:LongTermDebtCurrent at 2026-01-25.
- **Debt to equity, FY2025: 0.107.** Arithmetic: (8,463.0 + 0.0) / 79,327.0.
  - Inputs are us-gaap:LongTermDebtNoncurrent and us-gaap:LongTermDebtCurrent at 2025-01-26.
- Leverage roughly halved. Debt edged down while equity nearly doubled.

#### Cash flow
| Ratio | Value | Arithmetic |
|---|---|---|
| Free cash flow, FY2026 | $96,676.0M | 102,718.0 - 6,042.0 |
| Free cash flow, FY2025 | $60,853.0M | 64,089.0 - 3,236.0 |
| Free cash flow growth | 58.87% | (102,718.0 - 6,042.0) / (64,089.0 - 3,236.0) - 1 |
| Free cash flow margin, FY2026 | 44.77% | (102,718.0 - 6,042.0) / 215,938.0 |
| Free cash flow / net income, FY2026 | 0.81 | (102,718.0 - 6,042.0) / 120,067.0 |

Free cash flow grew 58.87%, more slowly than net income at 64.75%. Free cash flow covered 0.81 of net income. Cash conversion was strong in absolute terms, but it ran behind reported earnings in fiscal 2026.
financial_analyst.latest_quarter:
### Third quarter of fiscal 2027 (three months ended October 25, 2026)

**Source:** 8-K accession 0001045810-26-000088, Item 2.02, Exhibit 99.1, accepted 2026-11-17 16:20:51 ET. The statement is in millions, except per share data, and is unaudited.

Release header: "Three Months Ended | Nine Months Ended / October 25, | October 26, | October 25, | October 26, / 2026 | 2025 | 2026 | 2025". This quarter is the column for 2026. The same quarter last year is the column for 2025.

#### Revenue
- Release line: "Revenue | $115,844 | $57,006 | $293,681 | $147,811".
- Quarter revenue: $115,844 million, against $57,006 million in the same quarter last year.
- **Growth on the same quarter last year: 103.21%.** Arithmetic: 115,844 / 57,006 - 1, computed in code.
- This matches the release's rounded statement: "revenue for the third quarter ended October 25, 2026, of $115.8 billion, up 20% from the previous quarter and up 103% from a year ago."

#### GAAP diluted EPS
- Release lines: "Net income per share:" followed by "Diluted | $2.70 | $1.30 | $7.55 | $3.14".
- Quarter GAAP diluted EPS: $2.70, against $1.30 in the same quarter last year.
- **Growth: 107.69%.** Arithmetic: 2.70 / 1.30 - 1, computed in code.
- The release also gives non-GAAP diluted EPS: "GAAP and non-GAAP earnings per diluted share were $2.70 and $2.68, respectively." I used the GAAP figure of $2.70.

#### Other release figures (quoted, not recomputed)
- "GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were 74.8% and 74.9%, respectively."
- Nine-month GAAP diluted EPS was $7.55, against $3.14 a year earlier (diluted line above).
- Nine-month revenue was $293,681 million, against $147,811 million (revenue line above).

financial_analyst.valuation:
### Valuation

- **P/E: 31.7.** Arithmetic: 155.46 / 4.90 (price / diluted EPS).
  - Price: $155.46, the close of 2026-11-17, from financialdatasets.ai. It is the last close before the release was accepted at 2026-11-17 16:20:51 ET.
  - EPS: fiscal 2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $4.90, from us-gaap:EarningsPerShareDiluted, 2025-01-27 to 2026-01-25, 10-K 0001045810-26-000021.

#### Caveat on the denominator
- The EPS in this P/E is for the fiscal year that ended 2026-01-25. The price date is almost ten months later.
- Since then, the company has reported nine-month fiscal 2027 GAAP diluted EPS of $7.55, and $2.70 for the third quarter alone (release line "Diluted | $2.70 | $1.30 | $7.55 | $3.14").
- On trailing-twelve-month earnings the P/E would therefore be materially lower than 31.7.
- The context does not hold a trailing-twelve-month EPS, and I cannot compute one from calculator_variables, so I give no figure for it.

#### What the ratios say
- The 31.7 multiple sits against these fiscal 2026 results:
  - GAAP diluted EPS growth of 66.67%
  - Operating margin of 60.38%
  - Return on average equity of 101.49%
  - Debt to equity of 0.054
  - Free cash flow of $96,676.0M
- The latest quarter shows growth still accelerating on a year-over-year basis: revenue up 103.21% and GAAP diluted EPS up 107.69%.
- There are no peers in the context, so I cannot place the multiple relative to the sector.
- I have requested an earnings yield (diluted_eps / price) in calculator_requests.
- No recommendation is given.
definitions: Revenue is total revenue as tagged us-gaap:Revenues in the fiscal 2026 10-K; the context offers no separate net sales figure.
Net income is net income attributable to the parent (us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss).
EPS is GAAP diluted EPS (us-gaap:EarningsPerShareDiluted for the year; the release's GAAP 'Diluted' line for the quarter), not the release's non-GAAP diluted EPS of $2.68.
Return on equity is on average equity: the mean of stockholders' equity at 2026-01-25 and 2025-01-26 (us-gaap:StockholdersEquity), not year-end equity.

Debt is long-term debt excluding current maturities (us-gaap:LongTermDebtNoncurrent) plus current maturities (us-gaap:LongTermDebtCurrent); it excludes lease liabilities, which are not in the context.
Free cash flow is cash from operations (us-gaap:NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities) minus additions to property and equipment, taken from us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets.
Operating margin is operating income (us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss) divided by total revenue (us-gaap:Revenues).
P/E uses the 2026-11-17 closing price over fiscal 2026 (year ended 2026-01-25) GAAP diluted EPS, not trailing-twelve-month or adjusted EPS.

context.release_first_paragraph:
NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Third Quarter Fiscal 2027
•Revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year ago
•Data Center revenue of $107.6 billion, up 110% from a year ago
•Vera Rubin NVL72, the most versatile and advanced computing platform ever built, has shipped
SANTA CLARA, Calif.—Nov. 17, 2026―NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today reported revenue for the third quarter ended October 25, 2026, of $115.8 billion, up 20% from the previous quarter and up 103% from a year ago. For the quarter, GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were 74.8% and 74.9%, respectively. GAAP and non-GAAP earnings per diluted share were $2.70 and $2.68, respectively.
“Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” said Colette Kress, interim CEO and executive vice president and chief financial officer of NVIDIA. “Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater.”
In September 2026, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors approved an increase of $150 billion to the company’s share repurchase authorization, without expiration. During the third quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA returned $28.1 billion to shareholders in the form of shares repurchased and cash dividends. As of the end of the third quarter, the company had approximately $227.3 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization.

output.thesis: NVIDIA trades at a **P/E of 31.7** on fiscal 2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $4.90. The company has already reported nine-month fiscal 2027 GAAP diluted EPS of $7.55, so on trailing earnings the multiple is materially lower than 31.7. Growth is still accelerating: third-quarter revenue of $115,844 million was up 103.21%, and GAAP diluted EPS of $2.70 was up 107.69% from $1.30. The business also funds itself with ease, with fiscal 2026 free cash flow of $96,676.0M and debt to equity of 0.054. The main risks are that operating margin narrowed from 62.42% to 60.38% and that revenue is concentrated, with one direct customer at 22% and another at 14% of fiscal 2026 revenue.
output.what_would_change_it: We would move to Hold if next-quarter revenue fell short of management's guidance of "$130.0 billion, plus or minus 3%" or if operating margin kept narrowing below 60.38%. A pullback in spending by the direct customer that accounted for 22% of total revenue would also change the recommendation.
strategic_recommendations: Check next quarter's revenue against management's guidance: "Revenue is expected to be $130.0 billion, plus or minus 3%."
Track customer concentration: in fiscal year 2026, one direct customer represented 22% and another 14% of total revenue, so any capex cut by these customers is the key single-name risk.

Follow the Vera Rubin ramp and its promised "up to a 10x reduction in cost per token compared to Blackwell", because NVIDIA remains "effectively foreclosed" from China's data center compute market while competitors build ecosystems there.
